minutes_text:
CITY OF GLENDALE
  BLUE RIBBON PENSION REVIEW EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE
  SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES

  October 11, 2021

ROLL CALL

Present: Amirian, Bain, Michals, Molano, Finch
Staff: Doyle, Takhtalian, Martirosian, Hovsepian, Bradford, Cerritos, Jensen, Holtzman,
Soghomonyan

1. REGULAR BUSINESS AGENDA
  a. Report of Recorder, re: Posting of Agenda. Mr. Soghomonyan reported that
  the Agenda for the October 11, 2021 Special Meeting of the Blue-Ribbon
  Pension Review Committee was Posted on October 8, 2021, on the Bulletin
  Board Outside City Hall.
2. MINUTES
  None.
3. BUSINESS ITEMS
  a. Future Committee Agenda Items
Holtzman begins by discussing his ideas for future items. Holtzman suggests having
one session lead by John Bartel to discuss the City’s long-term forecast, options for
alternatives, and information on the population or retirees in the City. Molano suggests it
would be good to have presenters who haven’t worked with the City before, for
example: Former State Senator Jon Moorlach, Former City Manager of Santa Monica,
Former City Manager of Pasadena Rick Cole, attorney John Stephens (active member
of Costa Mesa pension committee), a member of Glendale’s taxpayer association, City
Treasurer Rafi Manoukin, and a representative from CalPERS management. Bain likes
the idea of having John Bartel start off the presentations with an overview and a
discussion of the limits on what can and cannot be done. Bain also suggests bringing
legislators in near the end of the Committee’s tenure. Molano requests that Doyle
explains how past abuses of the pension system have been perpetrated. Doyle states
that Glendale has not seen or tolerated any of the abuses that he has seen in other
cities. He explains that employee compensation is in most cases negotiated and subject
to the collective bargaining process; there is very little opportunity for spiking, and it is
not something that would be tolerated.

Michals notes that he would like to see a presentation from Bartel going into detail as a
starting point for the Committee and the public so that, when the Committee starts
discussing solutions, the Committee and public have a solid background. Amirian
agrees with Michals and Bain; he thinks that hearing from Bartel would lay out a very
good foundation, after which he is open to having more speakers come in to provide
additional context. Amirian adds that he thinks there are certain things the Committee

  1
 does not have the power to do and that it should not waste its time pursuing those
things, e.g., options that would violate current collective bargaining agreements. Finch
agrees with suggestion of starting with Bartel.

Holtzman suggests that the committee should start with a foundation of information,
then discussion of critiques, and then a discussion of solutions.
Molano expresses a worry about the presentations being too long and too dull or
complicated for the average viewer and would like the presentations to have summaries
that give a big picture of the presentation. Holtzman agrees that this is challenge. Bain
notes that he is hoping to bring to the committee some underlying concepts that make
things easier to understand.
Molano suggests that the Committee needs to communicate to the public about what
the City’s pension obligations and expenses mean for taxpayers.

Michals requests that the Executive Committee give Holtzman leeway at this stage to
develop agenda items for the Committee, given that the Executive Committee is around
to provide criticism and adjust course if necessary.

Holtzman would like to get discussion on vested rights and a presentation from
CalPERS management in early in the tenure of the Committee.

Bain requests that Bartel focus on translating percentages into dollar amounts so that
the lay person can understand the significance. Molano adds that those numbers be
made relative to the number of residences in the city, approx. 75,000 households.
Molano explains that costs associated with pension obligations should be discussed in
those terms because that will allow the residents of Glendale to understand the
situation.

Molano requests that the Committee account for the long-term costs associated with
increases in compensation for employees. Finch expresses that hearing Staff’s
presentation last week was extremely helpful in laying a groundwork. She likes the idea
of Holtzman securing presenters to give us a foundation of information, and then
critiques, and then possible solutions.

Molano suggests that the Committee consider the financial impact to the City over the
last 20 years, not just the debt accumulated, but also deficiencies in infrastructure and
deferred capital improvements. Holtzman agrees that he wants to assess the future
costs to the City but notes that it’s hard to do a forensic analysis of the past to
determine in any specificity the impact that pension costs had on infrastructure and
deferred capital improvements.

Amirian expresses an interest in having summaries of presentations that will be
accessible to the public and reiterates Michal’s suggestion to give Holtzman the

  2
 opportunity to decide who the Committee needs to hear from and lay the foundation for
future work to be done by the Executive Committee and the Committee at large.

Molano provides a list of items that he would like the Committee to discuss during its
tenure:
  o 20 years of data on the City’s CalPERS expenses
  o Financial impact over last 20 years
  o Public awareness and transparency regarding pension obligations
  o Testimony from Director of Finance to give overview
  o History of CalPERS
  o Explanation of abuses and arrangements of pension calculations
  o Market rates of return and impact of recessions
  o Evaluation of income and retirements of Glendale as a whole
  o Issue of how Pension Committee moves forward
  o
Molano notes that he concerned about there being a conflict of interest with having City
employees as members of the Committee. He suggests they should they be ex-officio
members instead.

Holtzman responds by explaining that the general rule from the Brown Act is that
something which affects all city employees does not pose a legal conflict of interest.
Martirosian also notes that because the end result of the Committee is an informational
report, there is no conflict of interest.

  b. Scheduling Executive Committee Meetings

The Executive Committee members discuss the schedule for future meetings. Molano
expresses an interest in having an Executive Committee meeting after each regular
Committee meeting. Michals, Amirian and Bain disagree and think that once a month is
sufficient for now. The members decide to start with having one Executive Committee
meeting per month, starting on November 5, 2021.

Finch proposes that the next meeting to start with questions about the City’s
presentation from the previous week. Holtzman agrees and suggests adding something
other than John Bartel’s presentation to that session. Michals suggests that the
committee designate a time for questions for other meetings as well. Holtzman suggests
30 minutes for questions. Finch, Molano and Michals agree. Holtzman and Takhtalian
suggest that questions be given to Holtzman and Staff before the meetings take place.
Holtzman asks that the questions go to him before the session and that members make
sure not to reply-all.

4. REPORTS - INFORMATION ONLY
none
5. REQUESTS FOR ITEMS ON FUTURE AGENDAS

  3
 none
6. ADJOURNMENT

Molano motions to adjourns
Finch Seconds

Meeting adjourns at 8pm.
